extracted.intended_audience: community and non-transient non-community water system owners/operators and State regulators responsible for implementing the EPA Lead and Copper Rule
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory reporting and recordkeeping requirements that water systems must follow for lead and copper monitoring, service line inventories/replacement, public education, treatment changes, and related laboratory certification under the EPA Lead and Copper Rule subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory performance evaluation and certification requirements for lead and copper
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must analyze Performance Evaluation samples that include lead and copper provided by or acceptable to EPA or the State at least once a year by each method for which the laboratory desires certification; achieve quantitative acceptance limits; achieve method detection limit for lead; and be currently certified by EPA or the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance limits: For lead ±30% of the actual amount in the PE sample when the actual amount ≥ 0.005 mg/L (PQL for lead = 0.005 mg/L). For copper ±10% when the actual amount ≥ 0.050 mg/L (PQL for copper = 0.050 mg/L). Method detection limit (MDL) for lead = 0.001 mg/L (procedures in appendix B of part 136). Laboratories must be currently certified to perform analyses to the specifications described. States may allow previously collected monitoring data if collected and analyzed per this subpart. Reporting convention: levels between PQL and MDL may be reported as measured or as one-half the PQL; levels below MDL must be reported as zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site sample plan and sample collection instructions submission and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: By the start of a system's first lead and copper tap monitoring period, water systems must submit to the State a site sample plan listing tap sample site locations (identified from the service line inventory) and tap sampling/entry point sites for water quality parameter monitoring; and a copy of the sample collection instructions provided to individuals who are sampling (meeting §141.86(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to the site sample plan require submission of an updated plan to the State before the next tap sampling period; the State may require modifications. If the system seeks to modify sample collection instructions, the updated version must be submitted to the State for review prior to the next sampling period. Systems with lead, galvanized requiring replacement, and/or lead status unknown service lines must evaluate tap sampling locations prior to each tap sampling period and submit updates if changes occur. If a system cannot identify enough eligible sampling sites, it must submit documentation (including customer refusal documentation) to support that conclusion prior to the next tap sampling period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tap monitoring reporting contents and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For all lead and copper tap samples and required water quality parameter distribution/entry point samples, a water system must report specified information to the State within the first 10 days following the end of each applicable sampling period (unless State specifies earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items to report: (i) results of all tap samples (including first- and fifth-liter where applicable), site locations, and site selection criteria used; (ii) documentation for each tap sample for which invalidation is requested; (iii) certification (except for initial tap sampling) that prior monitoring results were made publicly accessible; (iv) the 90th percentile lead and copper concentrations calculated per §141.80(c)(3) unless the State calculates them; (v) identification and explanation for any site not sampled during the previous period; (vi) results of all tap samples for required water quality parameters (§141.87(b)-(d)); (vii) results of all entry point samples for applicable water quality parameters; (viii) number of sites where customer participation was non-responsive after two attempts or refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute sample documentation for insufficient stagnation time
rubrics_metrics.description: When a non-transient non-community or qualifying community water system does not have enough taps that can provide first- or first-and-fifth-liter paired samples meeting the six-hour minimum stagnation time, the system must either provide documentation identifying standing times/locations for substitute samples or, if the State waived prior approval, identify each site that did not meet six-hour stagnation and provide the actual standing times with the sample results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must provide this documentation by the start of the first applicable tap monitoring period, or prior to the next tap sampling period if changes occur. If the State has waived prior approval, the substitution details must accompany the lead and copper tap sample results as required in paragraph (a)(2)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and approval requirement for new source or long-term treatment changes
rubrics_metrics.description: At a time specified by the State, or if none specified, as early as possible but no later than six months prior to the addition of a new source or any long-term change in water treatment, a water system must submit written documentation describing the addition or change to the State and obtain State approval before implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may not implement the addition of a new source or long-term treatment change without State approval. The State may require actions before or after the change (e.g., additional monitoring, additional tap sampling, re-evaluation of corrosion control). Examples of long-term changes include addition or modification of treatment processes, switching disinfectants or coagulants, or switching corrosion inhibitor products; short-term daily fluctuations are not considered long-term changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring waiver documentation and notification obligations for small systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 3,300 or fewer persons applying for or subject to a monitoring waiver must provide documentation to the State demonstrating they meet the waiver criteria by the start of their first applicable tap monitoring period and provide required information prior to each tap monitoring period to maintain the waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, within 60 days after becoming aware that the system is no longer free of lead- and/or copper-containing material (as appropriate), the system must notify the State in writing describing the circumstances and planned corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground water systems limiting entry-point monitoring must justify selected sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ground water system that limits water quality parameter monitoring to a subset of entry points must provide written correspondence to the State by the commencement of such monitoring identifying the selected entry points and including information sufficient to demonstrate that the sites are representative of water quality and treatment conditions throughout the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation must be provided at the start of the entry-point monitoring period specified in §141.87(b)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water monitoring reporting requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system must report source water monitoring results within the first 10 days following the end of each source water monitoring period specified in §141.88.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required to report: (1) sampling results for all source water samples collected in accordance with §141.88; (2) except for the first round of sampling, identify any site not sampled during the previous monitoring period and explain why the sampling point changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrosion control treatment reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: By the applicable dates under §141.81, systems must report specified corrosion control treatment information to the State depending on their status (optimized OCCT, required to optimize, required to evaluate, required to install or re-optimize, or exempt from certain steps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (1) systems demonstrating they have already optimized OCCT without State-set optimized water quality parameters must submit information required in §141.81(b)(1)-(3); (2) systems required to optimize must submit their recommendation regarding optimal corrosion control treatment (§141.82(a)); (3) systems required to evaluate effectiveness must submit required evaluation information (§141.82(c)); (4) systems required to install OCCT or re-optimized OCCT must submit a letter certifying completion of installation; (5) systems not required to complete §141.81(f) steps must certify completion of mandatory service line replacement program or that they met the minimum annual replacement rate under §141.81(f)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: By the applicable dates in §141.83, systems must provide source water treatment recommendations and completion certifications when required by §141.83.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required under §141.83(b)(1), provide recommendation regarding source water treatment; if required to install source water treatment under §141.83(b)(2), provide a letter certifying completion of the designated treatment within 24 months after State designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and baseline service line inventory reporting (timing and contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must submit an initial inventory of service lines (by Oct 16, 2024) and a baseline inventory by the compliance date that include counts of lead service lines, galvanized requiring replacement, lead status unknown, and other specified connector counts, counting each full shared service line only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial inventory must include number of lead lines, galvanized requiring replacement, and lead status unknown. Baseline inventory must include totals for lead, galvanized requiring replacement, lead status unknown, non-lead service lines, lead connectors, and connectors of unknown material, and count shared ownership lines only once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line replacement plan submission and annual update certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system that has inventoried one or more lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines must submit a service line replacement plan to the State by the compliance date and certify annually whether updates occurred (and provide updated plans if they did).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By January 30 after the end of the first program year, and annually thereafter, systems must either certify there have been no updates or submit an updated replacement plan. Systems may provide instructions on how to access the updated plan online instead of submitting the entire plan. Systems replacing lines under deferred deadlines must meet additional submission requirements per §141.84(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual inventory updates and discovery notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must provide the State with an updated inventory by January 30 after the end of the first program year and annually thereafter; inventories must conform to §141.84(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a system demonstrates the inventory contains no lead/galvanized requiring replacement/lead status unknown lines and known lead connectors/connectors of unknown material, it is no longer required to submit inventory updates except when it subsequently discovers such lines or connectors; in that case the system must notify the State within 60 days of discovery and prepare an updated inventory on a State-established schedule. Systems must provide service line material identification and replacement info if providing access instructions instead of a fixed copy of the inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual certifications for connector replacement and notification/mitigation activities
rubrics_metrics.description: By January 30 after the end of the first program year, and annually thereafter, systems must certify to the State that they replaced any encountered lead connectors per §141.84(e) or that none were encountered, and that they conducted notification and mitigation requirements for any partial and full replacements per §141.84(h), or that no replacements occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These certifications are required annually and must reflect whether actions occurred and compliance with procedural requirements for notification and mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of customer-initiated replacement activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report information about customer-initiated lead and galvanized requiring replacement service line replacements and certify completion per §141.84(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annually by January 30 systems must certify that all customer-initiated replacements were completed in accordance with §141.84(f). If the system cannot meet the 45-day deadline to complete a customer-initiated replacement, it must notify the State within 30 days following the replacement deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for mandatory service line replacement activities (detailed inventory outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems conducting mandatory service line replacement must submit, annually by January 30, detailed summary information from the most recent updated inventory including counts and addresses of replaced lines, connectors replaced/removed, replacement pool sizes, discoveries of miscategorized lines, deadlines and expected completion dates, and number of lines not replaced due to lack of access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items (per paragraph (e)(8)(i)-(ix)) include: total numbers of lead, galvanized requiring replacement, lead status unknown, non-lead service lines, lead connectors, connectors of unknown material (count shared lines once); totals and addresses for full and partial replacements in the preceding program year; total number and addresses of lead connectors replaced/removed; number of service lines in replacement pool at beginning of preceding year; number of lead status unknown lines determined non-lead in preceding year; addresses of non-lead lines later discovered to be lead or galvanized requiring replacement and the original categorization methods; applicable replacement deadlines and expected completion dates; and total number of lead/galvanized requiring replacement lines not replaced due to lack of access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line inventory validation reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems validating inventories pursuant to §141.84(b)(5) must submit a list of locations of any non-lead service lines identified to be lead or galvanized requiring replacement and the method(s) used to categorize service lines as a result of the assessment, and must submit the specific version/date of the inventory used in validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system may not use an inventory older than the inventory update submitted to the State at the start of the year in which the validation pool was determined. Validation information must be submitted no later than January 30 following seven years after the compliance date unless the State specifies otherwise. Documentation of previous validation efforts may be submitted by the compliance date for approval by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for service lines not replaced due to lack of access and reasonable-effort records
rubrics_metrics.description: By January 30 after the end of the first program year and annually thereafter, systems must submit documentation of the reasons for each service line not replaced due to lack of access, and documentation of reasonable efforts where the system was unable to obtain property owner consent if consent is required by State or local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must comply with the requirements of §141.84(d)(2) and (3) and be provided annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-replacement sampling and inspection reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that collect samples following partial or full lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line replacements required by §141.84(h) must report the results to the State within the first ten days following the month in which the system receives the results and any additional information the State specifies to verify replacement activities. Systems must also certify annually that they offered to inspect service lines when consumers suspected miscategorization within 30 days of receiving notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must report results in the time and manner prescribed by the State and provide verification information for partial replacements. Annual certification requirements appear by January 30 after the first program year and annually thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education program reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system conducting public education requirements must submit copies of written public education materials to the State prior to delivery and, within 10 days after the end of each required public education period, send documentation to the State that the materials were delivered and certify compliance with content and delivery requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must provide: (1) all written public education materials prior to delivery (State may require pre-approval); (2) written documentation within 10 days after each public education period containing the materials delivered and a certification that they meet §141.85(a) content and §141.85(b) delivery requirements; (3) a list of media outlets and organizations to which materials were delivered (resubmission not required if no changes and certified); (4) example copies of consumer notification of tap results with certification of proper distribution schedule (within three months following end of tap sampling period for samples used to calculate 90th percentile and annually by Jan 30 for other tap samples); (5) annual certification and example copies of notification and service line information materials delivered to customers at service connections with lead/galvanized/unknown lines; (6) certification and example copy that notification to affected customers and filter compliance after any disturbance occurred (or that no disturbance occurred), and report number of disturbances requiring filters and number of filters provided; (7) annual certification of outreach activities if replacement rate not met, plus copy of outreach materials; (8) annual certification of distribution system and site assessment information and public education materials provided to State and local health departments; (9) submission of filter plan within 60 days after a second exceedance in a rolling five-year period; (10) semiannual certifications (Jan 30 and July 30) for systems meeting multiple exceedance criteria certifying filter compliance and outreach activities and reporting number of filters provided and outreach materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of additional monitoring data and customer follow-up refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system which collects more samples than the minimum required must report those results to the State within the first 10 days following the end of the applicable monitoring period. The system must also certify the number of customer refusals or non-responses for follow-up sampling and provide documentation explaining inability to collect follow-up samples within the first 10 days following the end of the applicable tap monitoring period in which an individual sample exceeded the action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes monitoring data for distribution system and site assessment pursuant to §§141.82(j) and 141.86(b)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of 90th percentile lead and copper concentrations when State calculates
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system is not required to report the 90th percentile lead and copper concentrations if the State has notified the system it will calculate the 90th percentile based on tap results submitted and the system provides the results of tap water samples no later than 10 days after the end of the tap sampling period, and provides required site/location information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System must provide: (i) results of all tap samples including location and site selection criteria used; (ii) identification of sampling sites used in current monitoring that were not sampled previously and explanation for changes. The State must provide results of the 90th percentile calculations in writing to the system within 15 days of the end of the tap sampling period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and certification requirements for schools and child care facility sampling and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems must provide a list of schools and child care facilities they serve (or certify none) by the compliance date and must report school sampling and outreach activities annually by January 30 beginning one year after the compliance date, including delivery of health-risk information and sampling/notification certifications for elementary and secondary schools per specified schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must: (1) provide list or certification of none served by compliance date and annually certify if none; (2) report lead analytical sampling results for schools/child care facilities within 30 days of receipt; (3) annually certify good faith efforts to identify schools/child care facilities served and delivery of health-risk information; (4) during first five years certify completion of notification and sampling requirements for elementary schools and child care facilities and provide lists/numbers/names of schools sampled, declined, non-responding, and outreach attempts; (5) for secondary schools provide similar certifications; (6) starting in year six certify completion of specified notification and sampling requirements; (7) certify that sampling results were provided to schools/facilities and local/State health departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for small system compliance flexibility options
rubrics_metrics.description: Small water systems (serving 3,300 or fewer) and non-transient non-community water systems implementing small-system compliance flexibility options must submit specified monitoring results and certifications within required timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For point-of-use (POU) device option: report results from required tap sampling no later than 10 days after the end of the tap sampling period; if corrective action is not completed within 30 days of a POU sample exceeding 0.010 mg/L, provide documentation within 30 days explaining why corrective action was not completed; unless waived by the State, provide documentation certifying maintenance of POU devices. For the option to replace all lead-bearing plumbing: provide certification to the State that all lead-bearing material has been replaced on the State-established schedule within one year of designation of the option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements and retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system subject to this subpart must retain on its premises original records of all sampling data and analyses, reports, surveys, letters, evaluations, schedules, State determinations, and any other information required by §§141.81–141.88, 141.90, 141.92, and 141.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All records required by this section must be retained for no fewer than 12 years.
